thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: gpu-pool 'gpu-prod-eu-1' queue length > 2k, tail latency rising above SLOs, autoscaler reported repeated scaling failures (x5)
Navin: paging oncall, I'm on it. Which customers are hitting this?
Erica: I'm pulling autoscaler logs now. looks like scale requests are being rejected by control plane with 'max_nodes_reached' and some rate-limited errors from the cluster API.
Sam: quick metric snapshot: queue=3200, inflight=1200, token_throttle=78%, throttle_rejections=11.7% in last 5m, median latency 850ms, p95 2.6s.
Julia: we had a config push 18m ago to batching and prefix cache as part of load-tuning. continuous_batching.max_delay bumped 8ms->80ms and prefix_cache.mode changed to 'lazy' (effectively disabled prefetch). suspect regression.
Navin: ok mark hypothesis: batching window increase caused larger batches but also bigger per-request latency and reduced throughput due to warm-cache churn. autoscaler couldn't keep up.
Erica: autoscaler traces: requests to provision GPUs returned 409 until ~5m ago. control-plane returned 'quota_exceeded' for new node pools. looks like we hit a hard cap on replica count (max_nodes=32).
Sam: customers affected: org-lyra (high-traffic), org-rivka (background embeddings) — CS already flagged errors.
CS-Lead: getting customer notices ready. status: degraded for text-generation endpoints in eu region, advising retry/backoff.
Navin: immediate mitigation plan: 1) revert the batching/prefix-cache config to previous commit 2) scale pool manually if possible 3) open emergency quota request with infra control plane.
Erica: trying a manual scale now via controller CLI: 
```
redwoodctl pools resize --name gpu-prod-eu-1 --replicas 36
```
Erica: CLI returned: ERROR: quota limit prevents resizing beyond 32. Need control-plane override.
Ryan: can we move some low-priority workloads to other pools (us-west) as a temporary freeload? Could be faster than quota request.
Sam: Yeah we have a couple non-critical batch jobs on the same pool. I can fence them out. Suggest marking them 'evict' and migrate.
Julia: I'm preparing a rollback patch for the config change. rolling batching/prefix-cache to previous good SHA: 8a7c4f2
Erica: applying rollback now via infra pipeline:
```
ci-deploy rollback --env prod --component serving-config --to 8a7c4f2
```
Erica: pipeline kicked off. will watch logs.
ops-bot: Deploy started by Erica. Job #9845. Watch: https://ci.redwood/jobs/9845
Sam: while rollback runs, I'm draining batch jobs with: 
```
kubectl label pods -l app=batch-workload evict=true --namespace gpu-workloads
```
Sam: evictions started, freeing ~4 GPUs in the next 30s.
Navin: opened emergency quota request with infra control plane: ticket #INC-5421 (requested +10 nodes). ETA unknown.
Erica: rollback completed, config now back to continuous_batching.max_delay=8ms and prefix_cache.mode=active. Restarting serving processes.
ops-bot: Service restart event: serving-runtime eu cluster rolling restart started by Erica.
Sam: seeing initial signals: queue dropping from 3200 -> 1800 in 90s, throttle_rejections down to 6%.
Julia: monitoring prefix cache hit-rate: pre-rollback hit-rate was 18%, now 79% and KV cache warmups happening.
Navin: control-plane just updated quota: we got temporary bump +6 nodes to unblock if needed.
Erica: manual scale applied to 36 replicas after quota bump:
```
redwoodctl pools resize --name gpu-prod-eu-1 --replicas 36 --reason "incident mitigation"
```
Erica: scale success. new capacity online.
Sam: p95 latency back to 320ms, median 140ms, queue 120, throttle 1.2%. markers trending to healthy.
CS-Lead: notifying impacted customers: sent short note to org-lyra and org-rivka. included ETA and mitigation steps.
Navin: root cause (preliminary): recent config change increased continuous_batching.max_delay and disabled proactive prefix cache prefetch. That combination increased request coalescing and cache churn; autoscaler was then triggered by high queue but blocked by configured max_nodes and a quota cap. The autoscaler retries hit rate limits.
Julia: action items: 1) revert config change permanently and add stronger gating for batching experiments (AB test flag + automated perf smoke tests) 2) add autoscaler health check that alerts when scale requests are repeatedly failing 3) add temporary safety margin on max_nodes or queue-based emergency fallback routing to other regions 4) postmortem and release notes.
Erica: creating incident ticket and assigning owners. Navin on infra follow-up, Julia on config gating, Sam on runbook updates, CS-Lead on customer follow-up.
Navin: oncall handoff in 40m — I'll document current status and hand to Ryan.
Ryan: taking handoff. leaving monitoring in place. if queue climbs >500 reopen page.
ops-bot: Incident incident-1779456789 marked 'resolved (mitigated)'. duration 00:10:11.
Sam: quick note for postmortem: include exact config diff and timeline, include autoscaler logs showing 'max_nodes_reached' and control-plane quota responses.
CS-Lead: we'll coordinate customer comms with legal if any escalations.
Navin: thanks everyone. closing the incident channel once runbook and postmortem ticket are created. :thumbsup:
